rfi.description: French modelling scout Daniel Siad, 69, who had close ties to convicted US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, has been found dead at his home outside Paris, prosecutors and his lawyer have said.

rfi.title: Fast-moving wildfire in southern France forces hundreds to flee
rfi.description: A fast-moving wildfire that broke out in the Var department in southern France has forced 400 people to flee their homes and burned more than 2,500 hectares – the latest in a string of fires amid three heatwaves since early June.

rfi.title: Gabon and France deepen industrial cooperation with Eramet manganese deal
rfi.description: French mining group Eramet is considering a major expansion of manganese processing in Gabon under an agreement that could strengthen the country’s industrial base, modernise its railway network and reduce its reliance on exports of unprocessed ore.

rfi.title: Germany looks to Azerbaijan as Armenia ties shift regional relationships
rfi.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev have signed a series of economic agreements aimed at deepening Berlin's access to Baku's gas reserves and transit routes. The deal comes as Germany works to diversify its energy supply, and as Azerbaijan balances a Europe-leaning Armenia against a recently repaired relationship with Moscow.

rfi.title: France’s emergency agriculture bill passed, amid divisions over pesticides
rfi.description: France’s National Assembly has approved an emergency agriculture bill after a tense overnight debate, clearing the way for the possible temporary return of two pesticides banned in the country but still authorised elsewhere in the European Union.

rfi.title: France and Germany move to tackle EU’s growing trade deficit with China
rfi.description: France and Germany are pressing for a stronger European Union response to China’s growing trade surplus and industrial overcapacity, as concerns mount over the impact on key European sectors.

rfi.title: Ukraine’s wartime unity put to the test by protests over military leadership
rfi.description: Protests over the dismissal of Ukraine’s reformist defence minister entered a fifth day on Monday, deepening a political crisis that has placed President Volodymyr Zelensky under mounting pressure to overhaul the country’s military leadership.

rfi.title: Countdown to the ballot: Zambia gears up for August elections
rfi.description: This week on Spotlight on Africa, we're heading to Zambia, where general elections are set to take place on the 13th August. Voters will go to the polls to elect a president, members of the National Assembly, councillors and council chairs. Incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema has already picked up endorsements from within his own camp, the UPND Alliance, the coalition that's held power since 2021. So what's at stake, and who's in the running?

rfi.title: Senegal's Faye backs former president Sall's bid for UN top job in U-turn
rfi.description: Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has endorsed former president Macky Sall's candidacy to become the next United Nations secretary-general, the foreign ministry said on Monday, giving his predecessor crucial backing from his home country despite deep political divisions.

rfi.title: Burnham becomes UK's seventh PM in a decade after Starmer resigns

rfi.description: Gabon's President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema begins a three-day official visit to France on Monday, underlining the close relationship between Paris and one of its few remaining key allies in Francophone Africa.

rfi.title: Ecowas appoints Senegal's Birame Diop to drive regional reforms
rfi.description: West African leaders have appointed Senegal's former defence minister, General Birame Diop, to lead the Economic Community of West African States Commission, placing a military figure with extensive United Nations peacekeeping experience at the helm as the bloc seeks to recover from the departure of three member states.

rfi.title: France’s controversial Ripost public disorder law faces final test
rfi.description: France’s controversial “Ripost” law, aimed at strengthening the state’s response to urban unrest and public disorder, is set to face a decisive test on Monday when a joint parliamentary committee will study versions adopted by the National Assembly and the Senate.

rfi.title: Madagascar's wave of disappearances exposes 'deeper institutional failings'
rfi.description: A recent surge in disappearances and violent killings on the Indian Ocean island of Madagascar has fuelled fears across the country and prompted the government to deploy hundreds of security personnel. Anti-corruption campaigner Ketakandriana Rafitoson, of Transparency International Initiative Madagascar, told RFI the violence reflects a broader "crisis of confidence" in the country's institutions.

Pour empêcher le moustique-tigre de transmettre des maladies comme la dengue ou le chikungunya, des pulvérisations d’insecticide sont de plus en plus souvent organisées. Qui décide et qui les mène ? Dans quels cas ? Les habitants des quartiers concernés doivent-ils donner leur accord ?

lemonde.title: En Chine, les amours lesbiennes interdites
lemonde.description: Jeunesse en milieux hostiles (2/6). En 2014, à Xiamen, en Chine, la photographe néerlandaise Sarah Mei Herman faisait la connaissance de quatre étudiantes lesbiennes. Au fil des années et de leurs changements de vie, elle n’a cessé de les suivre. Attentive à restituer dans ses portraits une vérité que ces jeunes femmes, confrontées au tabou de l’homosexualité dans la société chinoise, dérobent au regard des leurs le reste du temps.

france24fr.title: Psychose à Antananarivo : les autorités tentent de rassurer après les disparitions d'enfants
france24fr.description: Depuis fin juin, une vague de disparitions frappe la capitale malgache, touchant en majorité des enfants et des adolescents. Entre fugues, négligences et soupçons de meurtres, les autorités peinent à rassurer une population qui bascule dans la psychose.

france24fr.title: Épuisement, manque d’effectifs, problèmes matériels... Laurent Nunez répond à la colère des pompiers
france24fr.description: Épuisement, manque d'effectifs, problèmes matériels... Face aux syndicats de pompiers qui dénoncent l'insuffisance de leurs moyens après la mort de trois d'entre eux en deux semaines, le ministre de l'Intérieur a assuré mercredi en Gironde, où deux professionnels ont péri la veille, que la France "fait face" aux incendies.

france24fr.title: CAN 2032 : "le Burkina Faso, le Niger et le Mali auront leurs chances", assure la CAF
france24fr.description: Le président de la CAF s'est prononcé sur la candidature conjointe des pays de l'AES pour l'organisation de la CAN 2032. Pour Patrice Motsepe, les trois pays auront les mêmes chances que tous les autres pays.

france24fr.title: Au Liban, l'Unesco place la cité antique de Tyr sur la liste du patrimoine mondial en péril
france24fr.description: Dans le sud du Liban, les ruines antiques de Tyr, l'une des plus anciennes cités du monde méditerranéen, ont été inscrites mercredi par l'Unesco sur la liste du patrimoine mondial en péril. L'organisation onusienne invoque les dommages causés par les bombardements israéliens et les risques de nouvelles frappes.

france24fr.title: Des humains de plus en plus exposés au risque de feux
france24fr.description: L'exposition des populations au risque d'incendie a augmenté de 40% entre 2002 et 2021 selon une étude parue dans la revue Science. La faute à l'étalement urbain. La plus grande proximité avec les forêts favorise les départs de feu (90% sont d'origine humaine) et augmente aussi le risque de voir des logements brûler. Par ailleurs, plus de 85% des personnes exposées à un incendie sur cette période l'ont été en Afrique, avec une surreprésentation des régions de savane dans le sud du continent.

france24fr.title: Le russe n'est-il vraiment plus enseigné en France ?
france24fr.description: La langue russe ne serait plus enseignée en France, affirme un internaute sur les réseaux sociaux. S'il est exact qu'en 2026, aucun poste d'enseignant de russe n'a été proposé aux concours de recrutement de l'Éducation nationale, des cours existent toujours bien au collège et au lycée.

france24fr.title: Tour de France : Jasper Philipsen ouvre son compteur de victoire lors de la 17e étape
france24fr.description: Le coureur belge Jasper Philipsen a remporté mercredi la 17e étape ​à Voiron, dans le département de l'Isère, en réglant au sprint un groupe d'une petite trentaine de coureurs. ​Il décroche ainsi sa première victoire sur cette 113e édition du Tour de France.

france24fr.title: Près de 150 migrants morts ou disparus au large de la Mauritanie en une semaine
france24fr.description: Nouveau drame migratoire au large de la Mauritanie. Près de 150 personnes sont mortes ou portées disparues en tentant de rejoindre les îles Canaries. L'ONU appelle à renforcer les voies de migration sûres.

france24fr.title: Cette vidéo ne montre pas un bombardier B-52 américain abattu par l'Iran
france24fr.description: Une vidéo censée montrer un bombardier américain B-52 détruit par un missile iranien cumule plus de trois millions de vues sur X, relayée notamment par un compte pro-iranien. Mais certains détails visuels trahissent une fabrication artificielle.

france24fr.title: Gaza : Zohran Mamdani veut faire arrêter Benjamin Netanyahu
france24fr.description: Le maire de New York, Zohran Mamdani, a déclaré mardi que son administration n'avait pas la capacité juridique d'arrêter le premier ministre israélien Benyamin Netanyahou comme il l'envisageait, et a appelé les autorités fédérales américaines à agir.

france24fr.title: En Italie, la mort d'Abderrahim Fakir ravive le débat sur les violences policières
france24fr.description: La mort d’Abderrahim Fakir, ressortissant marocain de 42 ans, lors d’une interpellation policière à Bologne dimanche, suscite une vive émotion en Italie. Une vidéo montrant l’homme immobilisé au sol et appelant à l’aide a provoqué des manifestations, ravivé le débat sur les violences policières et déclenché une passe d’armes politique.

france24fr.title: Monique Barbut, symbole de la désillusion de la société civile et de l'écologie sous Macron
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron a usé beaucoup de ministres issus de la société civile depuis son arrivée à l'Élysée en 2017. Pour la plupart d'entre eux, la vie gouvernementale et son lot d'arbitrages s'est souvent avérée délicate à gérer. Et encore plus lorsque c'est le fauteuil de ministre de la Transition écologique qu'ils occupaient, à l'image de Monique Barbut.

france24fr.title: Le Lac Rose retrouve un peu de sa couleur et relance l’économie du sel
france24fr.description:
Au #Senegal, le Lac Rose retrouve sa couleur et relance le tourisme de la région. En 2022, ce lac emblématique avait perdu sa couleur et sa salinité à la suite d'inondations extrêmes, entraînant un effondrement de la fréquentation touristique. 
 
Depuis, ramasseurs de sel, artisans, ONG et commerçants se sont mobilisés pour financer des opérations de pompage afin d'évacuer l'excédent d'eau et relancer l'économie locale.

france24fr.title: Mykhaïlo Drapaty, le visage d’une nouvelle génération à la tête de l’armée ukrainienne
france24fr.description: Mykhaïlo Drapaty a été nommé mardi commandant en chef de l'armée ukrainienne par Volodymyr Zelensky. Réformateur et soucieux de ses troupes, ce stratège militaire expérimenté incarne un profil qui semble nettement différent de son prédécesseur Oleksandr Syrsky. Portrait de ce quadragénaire nouveau n°1 de l’armée en Ukraine.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : Mykhailo Drapatyi nommé nouveau commandant en chef de l'armée
france24fr.description: Le nom de Mykhailo Drapatyi figure parmi les plus importants aujourd'hui en Ukraine après sa nomination au poste de commandant en chef de l'armée. Il succède à Oleksandr Syrskyi, dont de nombreux manifestants réclamaient la démission. Qui est Mikhailo Drapatyi ? Son portrait signé Sérine Bey.

france24fr.title: Inde : la crise entre les jeunes "cafards" et le gouvernement se poursuit
france24fr.description: Le bras de fer s'est poursuivi ce 22 juillet en Inde entre la contestation des "cafards", déterminés à obtenir la tête du ministre de l'Education pour cause de fraudes aux examens universitaires, et le gouvernement qui a pour la première fois évoqué l'idée d'une réforme. Récit de Ludovic de Foucaud.

france24fr.title: Le Sénégal soutient désormais la candidature de Macky Sall à l'ONU
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, quelques jours après avoir reçu Macky Sall au palais présidentiel, le président Bassirou Diomaye a tranché ce lundi et a décidé d'appuyer la candidature de son prédécesseur au poste de secrétaire général des Nations unies. Ce soutien était resté en suspens jusqu'ici. Il est désormais officiel.

france24fr.title: Canicule de juin  : Santé publique France calcule un excès de près de 6 0000 décès dans l'Hexagone
france24fr.description: Dans un deuxième bilan sur la période caniculaire allant du 17 juin au 2 juillet, Santé publique France constate un excès de mortalité de 5 764 personnes par rapport aux données normales sur cette période. L'Ile-de-France est la région la plus touchée, alors que 98,5 % de la population hexagonale ont dû subir cet épisode inédit de canicule.

zeit.title: Verkehrskontrolle: Spülen statt pinkeln: Fahrer will Drogenkonsum verheimlichen
Flüchtlingspolitik: Bundesregierung ebnet Weg für mehr Abschiebungen nach Afghanistan
zeit.description: Künftig dürfen auch ausreisepflichtige Staatsangehörige ohne Vorstrafen nach Afghanistan abgeschoben werden. Das Bundesinnenministerium hob entsprechende Hürden auf.

zeit.title: Nuklearabkommen: US-Regierung unterzeichnet Atom-Deal mit Saudi-Arabien
Irankrieg: USA und Saudi-Arabien unterzeichnen Atomabkommen
zeit.description: Die US-Regierung will dem Königreich beim Aufbau eines zivilen Atomprogramms helfen. Im Irankrieg ist die Annäherung an Saudi-Arabien von Bedeutung. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Atom: US-Regierung genehmigt Atom-Deal mit Saudi-Arabien
Elektroauto-Vorreiter: Tesla verfehlt Gewinnerwartung der Wall Street
Stade: Sonderbeobachtung des Stade-Verdächtigen endete kurz vor dessen Tod
zeit.description: Eine Psychologin schätzte den mutmaßlichen Täter von Stade als nicht suizidgefährdet ein. Seine besondere Beobachtung wurde deshalb kurz vor seinem Suizid beendet.

zeit.title: Fußball-Bundesliga: Offiziell: Abwehrspieler Wöber wechselt zum FC Schalke 04
Landkreis Bergstraße: Frontalzusammenstoß auf B47 - acht Verletzte
Verschwörungstheorien in den USA: »Dieses Land gehört der Wall Street«
zeit.description: Alles sei Verschwörung: Nicht erst seit den Epstein-Files gibt es in den USA die Vorstellung, dass das Land von Menschen regiert wird, die gar nicht gewählt wurden.

zeit.title: Brennelemente-Produktion: Niedersachsen genehmigt Fertigung russischer Brennelemente in Lingen
zeit.description: Das niedersächsische Umweltministerium erlaubt unter Auflagen die Produktion von Brennelementen russischen Typs in Lingen. Gleichzeitig kritisiert es die Zusammenarbeit.

zeit.title: Nicolás Maduro: Prozess gegen Maduro und Flores in den USA beginnt im Juni 2027
zeit.description: Ein US-Gericht hat den Termin für den Prozess gegen den abgesetzten Präsidenten Venezuelas, Nicolás Maduro, festgelegt. Maduros Anwalt pocht auf dessen Immunität.

zeit.title: US-Filmstudios: EU-Kommission billigt Übernahme von Warner Brothers durch Paramount
zeit.description: Nur unter Auflagen stimmt die EU-Kommission der Übernahme von Warner Brothers durch Paramount zu. Paramount muss Anteile an einem Filmvertrieb abgeben.

observador.title: Há uma falha escondida sob Évora. O sismo de 3,7 denunciou-a
observador.description: A estrutura que provocou o abalo de 3,7 não está identificada, mapeada, nem caracterizada. Pertencerá ao sistema regional de falhas ativas de Arraiolos. E pode gerar sismos mais fortes, admite o IPMA.

observador.title: Lisboa aprova programa contra ruído do aeroporto
observador.description: Câmara aprovou regulamento do Programa Menos Ruído, com 2,8 milhões de euros para Lisboa. Oposição critica modelo de reembolso e valores que "não chegam a financiar uma janela por casa".

observador.title: Malformações não detetadas: MP arquiva caso de Leiria
observador.description: Mãe queixou-se das médicas por negligência após filha nascer em 2023 com três dedos na mão e deformações no pé. Advogada vai pedir abertura de instrução.

observador.title: Ucrânia pede reunião urgente do Conselho de Segurança da ONU
observador.description: O ministro dos Negócios Estrangeiros da Ucrânia alerta para os ataques russos a navios de carga civis e afirma que "a Rússia está a manter a segurança alimentar global como refém.".

observador.title: Zelensky reúne-se com Witkoff e Kushner para relançar paz
observador.description: Witkoff e Kushner estiveram em Kiev. Mediação estava parada desde o início da guerra no Médio Oriente. Syrsky foi substituído como comandante do exército ucraniano.

observador.title: 23h. Incêndio em Alijó, em Vila Real, obriga ao corte do IC5
observador.description: Numa altura em que há cerca perto de 500 bombeiros no terreno, o incêndio continua com duas frentes ativas. Ainda, ministro da Educação considera que tem condições para continuar no cargo.

observador.title: Aston Martin concebe um V12 Vanquish (só) para 50 clientes
observador.description: A Aston Martin lançou a edição limitada Vanquish 25, equipada com o V12 biturbo com 835 cv, de que vão ser fabricadas 50 unidades, 25 em forma de coupé e outras tantas Volante, o descapotável da gama.

observador.title: Ministro afirma que "obviamente há resistências" nas escolas
observador.description: Fernando Alexandre sugere que as resistências vêm de docentes que não apoiam a sua reforma orgânica ao Ministério. Até agora, só foram reportados 680 casos de desconformidades, revela.

observador.title: Trump: Irão "estará pronto em breve" para acordo
observador.description: Trump afirmou que o Irão será em breve forçado a aceitar um acordo nuclear, enquanto prosseguem os ataques entre os dois países. O Presidente norte-americano voltou ainda a ameaçar Teerão.

observador.title: Novo líder do Hamas exige retirada total de Israel de Gaza
observador.description: No primeiro discurso à população palestiniana, o novo chefe do Hamas listou quatro prioridades — e ignorou a exigência de depor as armas, obstáculo central ao cessar-fogo.

observador.title: Descoberto primeiro exossatélite fora do Sistema Solar
observador.description: Telescópio VLT, no Chile, identificou um "exossatélite" com pelo menos a massa de Júpiter. Anos de tentativas falhadas antecederam a confirmação publicada na Nature.

observador.title: Municípios pedem reforço do financiamento do OE2027
observador.description: Da iluminação pública às refeições escolares, os municípios querem isenções de IVA e uma compensação real pelos custos da descentralização, sobretudo na educação.

observador.title: A derrota para perceber o que se ganhou e tem de ganhar
observador.description: Com vários titulares de fora por terem jogado de manhã com o Penafiel, FC Porto chegou atrasado a Barcelos e saiu mesmo com a primeira derrota da pré-temporada num encontro com poucos destaques (1-0).

observador.title: Brasil dá 3,11 mil milhões a setores afetados pelos EUA
observador.description: "Plano Brasil Soberano III" disponibiliza créditos para sectores como aço, automóveis e calçado. Lula diz que país pode "sair fortalecido" e não abandona negociações.

observador.title: Sp. Braga vence na Sérvia com golo de Ricardo Horta
observador.description: Golo aos 67 minutos dá vantagem aos minhotos antes da segunda mão, em 30 de julho, em Braga. Eliminatória vale acesso à fase de liga da Liga Conferência.

observador.title: 22h. Ministro da Educação diz que houve alarmismo exagerado
observador.description: O ministro da Educação afirma que não desvaloriza a situação, mas acredita que ainda tem a confiança dos professores e das escolas. Ainda, Nuno Melo sai em defesa de Fernando Alexandre e Luís Neves.

observador.title: Advogados questionam validade da prova do atrelado de droga
observador.description: Advogados de arguidos acusados no processo alertam: a movimentação do atrelado para empresa de João Santos Carvalho pode inviabilizar a prova em julgamento.

observador.title: Rússia alarga recrutamento militar a condenados por crimes
observador.description: O Parlamento aprovou uma lei que permite recrutar presos por tráfico de droga ou crime organizado para a guerra. Em troca do serviço militar, os detidos podem ser isentos de penas criminais.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Kiew will Sitzung im Uno-Sicherheitsrat wegen angegriffener Schiffe +++  Die Marine der EU entert einen russischen Öltanker
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: Der Blick auf die Natur verschiebt den Blick auf das eigene Leben
nzz.description: Naturverbundenheit ist eine von 26 empirisch identifizierten Sinnquellen. Die Forscherin Tatjana Schnell erklärt, wer darin Erfüllung findet und wie man sich als Teil der Natur empfindet. Der Sinnimpuls.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Google-Mutter Alphabet übertrifft Erwartungen +++ Porsche-Aufsichtsrat unterstützt Sparpaket
LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Trump droht Iran mit Angriffen auf Brücken und Kraftwerke
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Finanzaffäre im Zürcher Oberland: Eine Kamera sorgt bei der Ustermer Polizei für einen Geldsegen – der Statthalter bezweifelt, dass die Bussen rechtens sind
nzz.description: Unsauber verbuchte Rechnungen, zweifelhafte Kontrollen bei einem Bahnübergang: In Uster brodelt es gewaltig. Der Stadtrat kündigt eigene Abklärungen an.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Der Staat muss sich aus dem Volkswagen-Konzern zurückziehen. Andernfalls ist der Konzern nicht zu retten
nzz.description: Die niedersächsische Landesregierung und die Metall-Gewerkschaft behindern die nötige Sanierung des Volkswagen-Konzerns. Um ihren Einfluss zu reduzieren, sollte das VW-Gesetz abgeschafft werden.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Toter Buckelwal: Bizarre Spekulationen nach mysteriösem Laborbericht
nzz.description: Die Saga um den als «Timmy» bekannten Buckelwal ist zu Ende. Ende März war die Wal-Kuh auf einer Sandbank in Schleswig-Holstein gestrandet. In einer aufwendigen Rettungsaktion hatte eine private Gruppe das Tier Anfang Mai in die Nordsee gebracht, wo es aus ungeklärt bleibenden Gründen starb.

nzz.title: «Wir dürfen als Finanzplatz nicht davon ausgehen, dass unser Spitzenplatz gesichert ist», sagt der Chef der Privatbank EFG
nzz.description: Der CEO Giorgio Pradelli hat mit EFG mehr Neugeld angezogen als prognostiziert. Doch der künftige Präsident der Bankiervereinigung warnt vor Selbstzufriedenheit. Die Schweiz brauche den Marktzugang zur EU.

nzz.title: Trump schockt mit Pharmazöllen – aber Lonza sieht darin eine Chance
nzz.description: Der Pharmahersteller Lonza wähnt sich dank seinem internationalen Produktionsnetz im Vorteil. Im neuen grossen Werk in Kalifornien hat er noch freie Kapazitäten.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Knapp 5800 Tote durch Hitzewelle im Juni in Frankreich +++ Waldbrände auf Sizilien weiten sich aus
nzz.description: Wo ist es zurzeit besonders heiss? Und welche sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Hier sind die neusten Meldungen zu Hitzerekorden, Dürren und Bränden in Europa zu finden.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Albert Rösti muss weg – und warme Wohnungen sollen weniger Miete kosten: Die Grünen sind die launigste Partei des Sommers
nzz.description: Hinter den Botschaften der Öko-Partei steckt die Angst vor der Klima-Apokalypse. Sie will mit Verboten zurück in die Steinzeit.

nzz.title: Ein KI-System von Open AI bricht aus seiner Testumgebung aus und hackt ein Unternehmen
nzz.description: Eine autonom handelnde KI von Open AI hat die Sicherheitsschranken überwunden und das KI-Unternehmen Hugging Face angegriffen. Ausgerechnet eine chinesische KI half bei der Verteidigung.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Ebola-Ausbruch in Zentralafrika: USA stellen Rückkehrer aus Kongo-Kinshasa vorübergehend unter Quarantäne +++ Knapp 1000 bestätigte Todesfälle
nzz.description: Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation (WHO) hat den Gesundheitsnotstand ausgerufen. Es werden weitere infizierte Personen erwartet. Hier sind die wichtigsten Antworten zum Ebola-Virus zu finden.

nzz.title: Diese geheime Nuklearanlage in Iran will Trump zerstören: Was verbirgt sich im «Spitzhackenberg»?
nzz.description: Der amerikanische Präsident hat wiederholt damit gedroht, den tief vergrabenen Komplex zu bombardieren. Doch es bleibt unklar, was sich im Bergmassiv befindet – und welchen Schaden die USA überhaupt anrichten könnten.

nzz.title: Die Schweizer Schwimmerinnen mit Jahrgang 2010 sind überdurchschnittlich gut. Besser als ihre Vorgängerinnen und erfolgreicher als die Jungs
nzz.description: Weshalb? Das hat verschiedene Gründe. Einer davon könnte die Corona-Zeit sein.

nzz.title: Entmachtet, aber entschlossen: Türkischer Oppositionspolitiker trotzt Erdogan mit neuer Partei
nzz.description: Der abgesetzte Chef der grössten türkischen Oppositionspartei CHP, Özgür Özel, will eine neue Partei gründen. Viele Fraktionsmitglieder dürften ihm folgen. Unklar bleibt, ob Özel sich gegen die türkische Justiz behaupten kann.

spiegel.title: Mexiko stellt 20 Strafanzeigen gegen USA wegen toter Migranten
spiegel.description: Die US-Behörde ICE geht teils brutal gegen Einwanderer vor, immer wieder kommt es zu Todesfällen. Mexikos Regierung will das nicht länger hinnehmen – und schreitet juristisch ein.

spiegel.title: Saudi-Arabien, Donald Trump und der Kronprinz: USA und Riad schließen Nukleardeal
spiegel.description: Donald Trump hat sich mit dem saudischen Kronprinzen auf einen Atom-Deal geeinigt. Die US-Regierung erhofft sich wirtschaftliche Profite und Jobs. Noch kann der Kongress allerdings ein Veto einlegen.

spiegel.title: Mexiko: Journalist in Restaurant erschossen
spiegel.description: Am Mittwoch ist erneut ein Reporter in Mexiko getötet worden. Das lateinamerikanische Land gilt als einer der gefährlichsten Orte für Journalisten.

spiegel.title: Brad Pitt: Nun will auch Brad Pitts viertes Kind seinen Namen ablegen
spiegel.description: Shiloh hat den Namen Pitt bereits gestrichen, Zahara und Maddox haben einen entsprechenden Antrag gestellt. Nun folgt auch Vivienne, das jüngste Kind von Brad Pitt.

spiegel.title: Andy Burnham: Kann der neue Briten-Premier die Weltpolitik einfach auslagern?
spiegel.description: Gaza, Ukraine, Trump: Mit außenpolitischer Expertise ist Andy Burnham bislang nicht aufgefallen. Nun will der neue britische Premier vieles offenbar einem erfahrenen Minister überlassen – Ed Miliband. Doch das dürfte kaum funktionieren.

spiegel.title: Fußball-Leidenschaft der Argentinier: Das Märchen vom Homo »Argressivus«
spiegel.description: Alle Welt redet über das »respektlose« Verhalten der argentinischen Nationalmannschaft beim WM-Finale. Haben die schon mal die Gewalt der Europäer gesehen?

spiegel.title: Stellenabbau bei Porsche: Aufsichtsrat stimmt Sparpaket zu
spiegel.description: Das »Zukunftspaket« für den Autobauer Porsche hat eine weitere Hürde geschafft: Der Aufsichtsrat hat seine Unterstützung zugesagt. Mehrere Tausend Stellen könnten beim Autobauer Porsche künftig wegfallen.

spiegel.title: Pete Hegseth: Senator nennt Verteidigungsminister im Iran-Streit »Versager«
spiegel.description: Wortgefecht im US-Senat: Verteidigungsminister Hegseth und Demokrat Peters liefern sich eine heftige Debatte über den Irankrieg – dann wird der Senator deutlich.

spiegel.title: Wissenschaft: Was das Buch »Luft« von Jens Soentgen über CO₂ und Corona-Debatten verrät
spiegel.description: Das fulminante Buch »Luft« von Jens Soentgen lässt einen verstehen, warum die Coronadebatte so schieflief – und Forschung besser übersetzt werden muss.

spiegel.title: USA: Donald Trump schürt erneut Zweifel an der Wahl 2020 vor den Midterms - Podcast
spiegel.description: In seiner Rede an die Nation wirft Donald Trump China erneut vor, die Wahl 2020 manipuliert zu haben. Belege liefert er keine. US-Korrespondent Marc Pitzke erklärt, warum der Vorwurf vor den Midterms mehr ist als nur Rhetorik.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Gefechte per Fernsteuerung in den Todeszonen
spiegel.description: Eine klare Frontlinie existiert nicht – dafür Todeszonen, in denen unbemannte Flugobjekte alles angreifen, was sich bewegt. Ukrainische Spezialisten entwickeln immer neue Drohnentypen, um russische Angreifer zu stoppen.

spiegel.title: Saudi-Arabien, Donald Trump und der Kronprinz: Wird Riad jetzt Atommacht?
spiegel.description: Der Irankrieg eskaliert wieder – da billigen die USA ein Nuklearabkommen mit Saudi-Arabien. Das Königreich ist der Erzfeind der Ajatollahs und kann jubeln. Israel war zumindest offiziell nicht eingebunden.

spiegel.title: Centinera: Strand in Kroatien wegen Abwasserrohrbruch tagelang gesperrt
spiegel.description: Bei Bauarbeiten ist auf der kroatischen Halbinsel Istrien ein Abwasserrohr beschädigt worden. Das Meer wies am Strand Centinera daraufhin eine erhöhte bakterielle Belastung auf. Nun gibt es Entwarnung.

spiegel.title: Frankreich meldet knapp 5800 zusätzliche Tote während Hitzewelle
spiegel.description: Extrem hohe Temperaturen setzen vor allem älteren Menschen zu. Neue Zahlen aus Frankreich zeigen, wie gefährlich der bisherige Sommer war. Den Großraum Paris hat es besonders hart getroffen.

spiegel.title: Rettungsschwimmerin im Kinder-Interview: »Jeder Mensch sollte schwimmen können«
spiegel.description: Ute Vogt ist die Präsidentin der DLRG. Die Kinderreporterinnen Charlotte und Paula sprechen mit ihr über Rettungsschwimmer, Badeunfälle und darüber, warum Deutschland zu wenig Schwimmbäder hat.

spiegel.title: Unterlassene Hilfeleistung: »Wer eingreift, schützt andere mit, zum Beispiel Angehörige«
spiegel.description: In Warnemünde schaute ein Paar wohl weg, als sich eine Frau das Leben nahm. Warum verhalten Menschen sich mal sozial, mal egoistisch? Die Neurowissenschaftlerin Grit Hein forscht dazu seit Jahren.

phys-org.title: Quantum internet leaves the lab with first real-world entanglement over busy telecom fiber
phys-org.description: Quantum information is notoriously fragile. Internet traffic is anything but. Yet Northwestern University scientists have demonstrated they can peacefully coexist inside the same fiber-optic cable.

phys-org.title: Light-driven chemistry method could create antiviral compound libraries 10 to 100 times larger within weeks
phys-org.description: As the world faces new and often untreatable viral threats, Simon Fraser University researchers have found a way to cut years off the time it takes to discover antiviral drugs. The new research enables scientists to quickly create large libraries of nucleoside analogs (NAs), compounds that mimic the building blocks of DNA and RNA and are widely used to treat cancer and viral infections such as HIV and hepatitis.

A team from KIT's Institute of Microstructure Technology (IMT) and the Suzhou Institute of Nano-tech and Nano-bionics (SINANO) at the Chinese Academy of Sciences has now demonstrated that flow at a water surface alone is sufficient to rotate a floating object in a fixed direction. phys-org.description: For cells to function properly, they must produce the right amount of each protein. It is a delicate balance: Both too little and too much can compromise essential cellular functions. A team from the University of Geneva (UNIGE) has now shown that even a modest excess of tubulin—the protein that assembles into microtubules, the cell's internal scaffolding—is enough to disrupt tissue architecture and reduce cell viability. phys-org.title: Reusable magnetic invention removes microplastics plus some PFAS from water
phys-org.description: Microplastics are an increasing global concern, with growing evidence of their presence in water systems. RMIT University researchers have developed a water treatment material that rapidly removes micro- and nanoplastics and some PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances), bringing the technology closer to real-world use. The invention builds on the team's 2022 breakthrough in microplastics removal, extending its performance to much smaller particles and more complex wastewater.

phys-org.title: Shifting weather patterns drive 55% of Europe's summer drought trend, study finds
phys-org.description: In a new study, researchers at Leipzig University have identified a major cause of the unusually severe summer soil drying and rising temperatures across Europe. They found that much of the trend can be attributed to changes in atmospheric circulation patterns—that is, shifts in the weather regimes that typically occur over Europe. phys-org.description: Researchers at Skoltech, together with a colleague from the Shanghai Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, working within the joint SIOM–Skoltech laboratory, have determined how to select the thickness and density of a plasma target so that a pulse passing through it retains its attosecond duration and high intensity. The results will help improve the design of plasma-based sources of ultraviolet and X-ray radiation used to study ultrafast processes in matter

phys-org.title: Neural networks unlock larger quantum simulations with lower computational costs
phys-org.description: In recent years, research using artificial intelligence to predict material properties has advanced rapidly. Neural network quantum Monte Carlo methods have attracted attention as highly accurate simulation techniques. However, their extremely high computational cost has limited their application to small molecular systems. This study introduces a new computational method that overcomes this limitation.

phys-org.title: Detecting the body's magnetic fields with a low-power Ramsey-based magnetometer
phys-org.description: Our bodies generate extremely weak magnetic fields as electric currents flow through the heart, brain and other tissues. These signals are used in magnetocardiography and magnetoencephalography to assess heart function and brain activity, respectively. These fields can be detected at room temperature using diamond sensors containing nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, in which a carbon atom is replaced by a nitrogen atom adjacent to an empty lattice site.

phys-org.title: Crowd reactions influence whether people receive controversial political messages positively or negatively
phys-org.description: Positive crowd reactions like applause and laughter can make controversial political messages more acceptable to viewers, according to new research by psychologist Dr. Carl Senior at Aston University. The research suggests that how broadcasters and content creators use applause, laughter and booing can subtly shape public perceptions of populist figures and divisive issues like immigration.

phys-org.title: AI and quantum chemistry combine to identify efficient blue OLED materials

While initially an expensive luxury, OLEDs are gradually becoming more financially accessible as the technology improves. phys-org.title: Why river management is so crucial to protecting one of world's most important wetlands
phys-org.description: A major new study led by Swansea University has shown that upstream river management, rather than local rainfall, is the primary driver of one of the world's most important wetlands. According to the research published in Scientific Reports, which analyzed more than two decades of satellite observations, the future of Iraq's Mesopotamian Marshes depends far more on the water flowing from the Tigris and Euphrates rivers than on rainfall.

phys-org.title: Creating the largest-ever database on floating ocean plastic using smart cameras
phys-org.description: The first five years (2019–2024) of operations of The Ocean Cleanup's Automated Debris Imaging System (ADIS) have been reviewed, and the findings have been published in Environmental Research Communications. In addition to reviewing the technology's performance, the study covers the initial 14,500 km2 of global ocean surface scanned for plastic debris and the more than 20,000 large floating objects it helped identify.

phys-org.title: CRISPR-Cas coordinates a layered bacterial defense network in innate immunity
phys-org.description: All cellular life—from humans to bacteria—possesses two layers of immunity: innate and adaptive. Scientists have long understood how these two types of immunity work together in higher organisms but not in the microbial world.

phys-org.title: Q&A: Listening with light—an innovative new technology for studying the seafloor
phys-org.description: The seafloor plays an important ecological and societal role. Understanding the processes that shape this environment will help guide conservation policy and decision-making about underwater infrastructure and geohazards.

phys-org.title: First ever reported cryo-EM visualization of E. coli TGT structure
phys-org.description: The enzyme tRNA-guanine transglycosylase (TGT) chemically modifies transfer RNA (tRNA) and plays a key role in how disease-causing bacteria control the production of proteins needed to cause infection. E. coli TGT is nearly identical to the one found in Shigella, which causes the intestinal infection shigellosis. phys-org.title: Are penalties in the US airline industry a deterrent or a 'price?'
phys-org.description: Many people drive more carefully for a while after receiving a traffic fine. But do large corporations, such as airlines, also change their behavior when they face financial penalties? We examine this question by studying penalties imposed in the United States for lengthy tarmac delays.

phys-org.title: New optical method follows single proteins as they shift shape
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Twente have developed an optical method that follows the shape changes of a single protein in liquid without attaching anything to it. It reads the protein's structure from its own molecular vibrations, free from the labels or tags that other techniques rely on. The method could help researchers study how proteins respond to drugs, toxins and other biomolecules. The paper is published in the journal ACS Nano.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

proj-syn.title: What the New UK Chancellor Means for the UK Economy
proj-syn.description: By appointing John Healey as chancellor of the exchequer, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has taken a calculated risk. If Healey can leverage his insider knowledge of the Treasury, pursue a bold, pro-growth agenda, and manage his defense-spending instincts, he may be able to provide the structural shake-up the UK economy needs.

proj-syn.title: Will Trump’s War With Canada Become Global?
proj-syn.description: For the first time, a great power has moved to price transboundary climate-driven harms–massive wildfires–and extract compensation unilaterally. What was previously a development, insurance, or emissions-accounting issue is now a security and trade dispute between two G7 economies, setting a precedent that others may try to follow.

proj-syn.title: America Is Closing the Door on Opportunity—and Talent
proj-syn.description: Viewed in isolation, the Trump administration's new, more restrictive student-visa policy may seem modest. But as part of a broader retreat from openness, it signals that the country once known for offering ambitious outsiders a chance to transform their lives is less willing to do so.

proj-syn.title: Large Language Models for Small Language Communities
proj-syn.description: Many developing economies cannot access large language models, most of which have been trained on datasets in English. To build scalable and inclusive LLMs for countries with minority languages, policymakers' best bet is to tap mobile network operators, with their armies of developers and data-processing capabilities.

proj-syn.title: The Epstein Class Was Made Offshore
proj-syn.description: The impunity of Jeffrey Epstein and his associates is the predictable upshot of unbridled wealth concentration, facilitated by the offshore financial system. In fact, that system represents the selective withdrawal by a privileged few from the rule of law, without the loss of any of its benefits.

proj-syn.title: A New Tool for Combating Human Trafficking
proj-syn.description: While human trafficking is mostly framed as a macro phenomenon, this does not fully explain how these criminal networks operate. Recognizing that trafficking corridors link specific source and destination localities offers a stronger basis for policy than a purely national approach or isolated interventions.

proj-syn.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly in Global Tax Negotiations
proj-syn.description: Ongoing negotiations at the United Nations offer the international community the best chance that it will have to ensure that global taxation authority is assigned fairly. With multinationals and the ultra-rich abusing the current system to minimize their tax payments, finalizing a new convention is an urgent priority.

proj-syn.title: The Bayer Truth About Trump’s Farm and Food Policies
proj-syn.description: A new executive order on regenerative agriculture might seem to suggest that US President Donald Trump’s administration wants to help American farmers. But a closer look at the order and other recent developments reveals a familiar pattern: an unhappy public gets reassuring words, while corporate interests receive tangible support.

proj-syn.title: Don’t Overestimate America and China’s Importance
proj-syn.description: Some commentators on international affairs seem to think that “the West” and the BRICS+ do not really matter; only the United States and China do. Yet three factors complicate this simplistic framing, suggesting that even superpowers' influence has limits, and that smaller powers can sometimes punch above their weight.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s Rightward Turn
proj-syn.description: There is a growing tension in Colombia between the popular demand for a strong welfare state and a political system that cannot deliver on that promise unless it breaks free from malign influences. Since the incoming administration is aligned with many of those interests, Colombians will continue to be disappointed.

proj-syn.title: A Cold War Adventure in Portugal
proj-syn.description: Just 52 years after escaping military dictatorship, Portugal is an EU and eurozone member and the world’s seventh-safest country. While Donald Trump's systematic destruction of the rules-based global order will not reverse this progress, nor will it do any good for Portugal, the US, or anyone else.

proj-syn.title: Social-Media Age Bans Won’t Make Children Safer—But This Will
proj-syn.description: As the European Union considers how to protect and empower young people in a digital world, it must resist the urge only to enact a ban on social media for young people. A more effective strategy would force tech companies to remove addictive features by holding them to product-liability standards—as with most other industries.

proj-syn.title: Who Will Sit Atop the Next World Order?
proj-syn.description: American hegemony has given way to a global order based on rivalry and competition among several major powers, where there is no longer a fixed, codified set of rules. Instead, there is only economic, technological, and military power—the likes of which China is amassing faster than many observers realize.

proj-syn.title: AI Will Supercharge Surveillance Capitalism
proj-syn.description: For too long, governments have stood by and allowed the creation of business models built on the commercial exploitation of users' personal data and that reward social and psychological manipulation. With the AI industry poised to replicate this model, policymakers must intervene before it is too late.

proj-syn.title: An Alternative History for America at 250
proj-syn.description: Commemorating the 250th anniversary of the United States requires an honest appraisal of not only its founding principles but also its racist and imperialist legacy. A clear-eyed assessment shows why many people in the Global South remain cynical about the country’s ability to live up to its ideals.

proj-syn.title: A Turning Point for African Industrialization
proj-syn.description: Building on the success of his mega-refinery in Lagos, Nigerian industrialist Aliko Dangote is in talks to construct a second one in collaboration with several East African countries. African leaders should learn from Dangote’s strategy of adding value to the continent’s natural resources and fostering cross-border cooperation.

proj-syn.title: Subsidies Do Not Explain China’s Competitiveness
proj-syn.description: Like every major economy, China uses industrial policy, and its subsidies have mattered. But subsidies are no longer the most convincing explanation for Chinese firms’ emergence as global leaders in industries that used to be the exclusive domain of advanced economies.
